# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 48 (Bu-Vb Pc48)
**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc48
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 48
**Title (English, from literature):** Going to see a mobilized army
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bu-vb-pc48
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
In modern analysis, Michael Radich highlights Pācittiyas 48–50 as barring even passing contact between the monastic Saṅgha and armed forces, reading military institutions as an arm of the broader socio-economic structure from which monastics withdraw [Radich 2007]. An English translation of the rule and its accompanying case material is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
The rule is widely attested across early Vinaya traditions. Within Pali literature, it directly corresponds to *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* Pācittiya 48 and *Parivāra* Pācittiya 48, with counterpart disciplinary provisions for nuns found in *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* Pācittiya 129, the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*, and the *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* [SuttaCentral]. Parallels survive in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions across the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Lokottaravāda, and Kāśyapīya lineages, as well as the *Upāliparipṛcchā* [SuttaCentral]. Computationally, DharmaNexus registers 640 text-reuse matches across 115 Pali texts, sharing extensive formulaic phrasing with adjacent army-related rules such as Pācittiyas 49 and 50, other Pācittiya rules (such as Pc 85 and Pc 56), and Khandhaka passages (Kd 1, Kd 3, Kd 13) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns the text with Tibetan canonical Vinaya commentaries, notably the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106) and the *Vinayasūtraṭīkā* (D4120) [DharmaNexus].
